video_title_guess: Stephen A. Smith on Shannon Sharpe, Loyalty, and the Importance of Real Friendships | Out The Mud

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.quote: Well, listen, we gonna stay close. Um, you know, what happened with Shannon was unfortunate and that's his business to tell. He's on always have a friend in me. My friendship, my brotherhood with him ain't going nowhere. The same applies to the Ryan Clarks, the Marcus Spears, the Big Perks of the world, you know, I rock with these cats. These I love these brothers and we gonna always be tight. When it come to Shannon, I will say this to you. I was always gonna keep in touch with him. Was always gonna check on him. I'm always want him back. The company knows I want him back. Now y'all gonna do what y'all gotta do because I'm the executive producer but I'm not an executive VP of the company. I have bosses to answer to. They have to make that decision. But they already know I want him back. If we could get him back, I want him back. I ain't apologizing for that to nobody. He was great for me. He was great to me. And I'm not gonna forget that. He was great for the show as well.
quotes.why_it_matters: Stephen A. Smith's candid admission of wanting Shannon Sharpe back, despite their professional separation, highlights the personal bonds that can form in high-profile sports media partnerships, mirroring the complexities of team dynamics and player movement in the NBA where personal relationships often influence professional decisions.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.quote: I'm seeing them talking to Shannon and Shannon's talking about people who hadn't called him. And he made sure to mention that I wasn't one of those people that I kept in touch, which I did. But I saw him because you get to know him, if you work with him every day like I did, and he got quiet when he was talking about people that he thought were his friends. And that suddenly they ain't know him. They ain't call him, they ain't return his call, they ain't want to be seen. And I saw the hurt on his face. He was hurt, bro. He was hurt. When he was just talking about, I saw, I just looked at him. And from that moment forward, I told my man over here that's rolled up in here with me and everything, I said, there will never go a month without him hearing from me. What's up? You good? Everything all right?
quotes.why_it_matters: Smith's vivid description of Shannon Sharpe's emotional hurt over perceived abandonment by friends after leaving ESPN illustrates the personal toll professional transitions can take, emphasizing the importance of loyalty and support within the competitive sports media landscape, a sentiment relatable to players navigating team changes.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.quote: Me venturing into the political realm, watching people turn against me. My inner circle has gotten tighter. And there's people that have turned against me that I thought were my friends and loved ones and turned their back on me, bro. And I'm not letting that go. I know Christian man, Jesus forgive. I'm not that. I'm not gonna be an enemy and go out and exact vengeance on it. No, nothing like that. But I'm like, you can't come back into my life with some of the shit that people have said about me because of what you think my politics are. You don't even know what you're talking about. You don't even have it right. But to think that about me and to say that about me and to turn your back on me like that. I don't care that you disagree. I don't care that you got an issue with something that I said. Talk to me. Don't be like, don't turn your back on me. Don't act like all of a sudden we ain't friends.
quotes.why_it_matters: Smith's strong condemnation of former friends who turned on him over political disagreements highlights the intense scrutiny and personal cost public figures in sports media face, underscoring the non-negotiable value of loyalty and direct communication, a dynamic often at play in NBA locker rooms and front offices.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.quote: It's a big deal, man. It's like me being here sitting here with y'all. I've always, you've always been good to me. You always been good to me, but I never really knew you that well. I just know a lot of people who know you and they all swear by you. And they good enough, I mean, KG, Big Perk. I mean, please, that's first of all, with me, that's all you need. KG and Big Perk with me, I'm good. It don't get realer than them, you know. So it's definitely that, but Zebo and I go back years, we always see each other. The love is consistent, man. And when you got something like that, you value that shit. It's like, yo, it's it's cool. What you need? Anything good? You straight? Good. That's all you need from people, man, because you know, when he sees me, it's the same thing. I don't change. Feelings are the same. I'm always, what's up?
quotes.why_it_matters: Smith emphasizes the importance of consistent loyalty and genuine relationships, citing respected figures like Kevin Garnett and Kendrick Perkins, which reflects the deep bonds and trust valued within the broader sports community, including NBA locker rooms and coaching staffs.
